method_note: Every fix here was watched red on the reviewer's own mutation before it landed, per hard rule 2. Mutations were applied in place to src/sec10k/web/static/index.html and reverted with `git checkout --` (the tree was clean at 5c44c4a), which is equivalent to the reviewer's scratch copy. resolutions.reproduced: Yes, exactly as reported. `deepLink();` moved from after the try/catch to the first line of `boot()` in src/sec10k/web/static/index.html -> `python3 -m evals.run --suite invariant` gives `[PASS] ui-deep-link`, suite 63/63 = 1.000, while `?fixture=aapl-2025&run=1` renders nothing: `$("#fx").options` is empty at that point, the membership guard returns, and the feature is a permanent silent no-op.
resolutions.fix: check_deep_link's `guard_expr`/`run_expr` pair (inert — guard-before-run is fixed by deepLink()'s own function text and cannot move) is replaced by a single `order` list asserting the whole dependency chain in file order: the `$("#fx").innerHTML = m.fixtures...` assignment, then the `deepLink();` call site, then the guard, then the run trigger. Each consecutive pair must be non-decreasing in position, so a step that moves ahead of what it depends on is red wherever it moved to. The options assignment was added to `wire` as well, so its DELETION is reported as a missing pin rather than as a confusing -1 ordering failure.

resolutions.reproduced: Yes, both halves. (a) banner: `role="status" aria-label="doc_status"` -> `role="status" aria-labelledby="no-such-id"` gives `[PASS] ui-banner-status-role`, invariant 63/63 = 1.000. (b) item region: `aria-label="Item ${esc(it.item)} extracted text"` -> `aria-labelledby="ghost-${esc(it.item)}"` gives `[PASS] ui-item-text-region` — the ghost form even satisfies `label_must_interpolate`.
resolutions.fix: `_named(attrs, live)` now takes the live file text and resolves IDREFs: an `aria-labelledby` is a name only if EVERY whitespace-separated token names an `id="…"` present in the same live file; a dangling reference returns "", i.e. no name. New `_why_unnamed(attrs)` keeps the two defects apart in the diagnostic (dangling reference vs no naming attribute at all). Both consumers, check_banner_status_role and check_item_text_region, pass their `text` through. Documented ceiling, deliberate: the NAME of a resolving reference is the referenced element's text, which is not statically reachable here, so the labelledby form answers "is it named" and not "what does it say" — the page uses aria-label everywhere, so nothing rides on it today.
resolutions.red_output_verbatim: banner: [FAIL] ui-banner-status-role, invariant 62/63 = 0.984 -- #banner: no accessible name — aria-labelledby='no-such-id' resolves to no id present in this file, so the computed name is empty. role=status alone leaves the region anonymous || item region: class="text md": no accessible name naming the item — aria-labelledby='ghost-${esc(it.item)}' resolves to no id present in this file, so the computed name is empty; and the same for class="text"

resolutions.reproduced: Yes, exactly as reported. `#go-fx` relabelled "Upload" and `#go-up` relabelled "Fixture" -> `[PASS] ui-mode-button-names`, invariant 63/63 = 1.000, with all three visible labels still reading `Extract`.
resolutions.fix: check_mode_button_names' `buttons` input becomes {id: substring the name must carry} — go-fx/fixture, go-up/upload, go-url/URL — and the button regex now captures the element's VISIBLE text as well as its attributes. Two clauses added on top of non-empty + distinct: each accessible name must contain (case-insensitively) the substring naming its own mode, and each must contain its own visible label, which is WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name — the rule that keeps a speech-input user's "click Extract" working once an aria-label is in play. A bare list is still accepted for `buttons` and means "no per-mode pin", so the check stays usable by a case that does not want the second clause.
resolutions.covered_by: evals/adversarial/ui-mode-button-names.json (invariant + fast), check `mode_button_names`, input key `buttons` as a map
resolutions.red_output_verbatim: [FAIL] ui-mode-button-names (adversarial, 0.0s) / [eval] suite 'invariant': 62/63 = 0.984 -- #go-fx: accessible name 'Upload' does not name its own mode ('fixture') — distinct names that point at the wrong mode are worse than no names; #go-fx: accessible name 'Upload' does not contain its visible label 'Extract' (WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name — speech input targets the word the user can see); #go-up: accessible name 'Fixture' does not name its own mode ('upload') — distinct names that point at the wrong mode are worse than no names; #go-up: accessible name 'Fixture' does not contain its visible label 'Extract' (WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name — speech input targets the word the user can see)
resolutions.note: The Label-in-Name clause is what lets the D10 row's reviewer-evidence claim ("correct ARIA is screen-reader correctness, not agent special-casing") be backed by the eval set rather than merely asserted, which the reviewer named as the gap.
